# S54 — Show the ork version and logo in the terminal: TUI, --version, doctor

Follows S53. The owner wants the ork version shown in the TUI (2026-10-20, from a screenshot of the Overview: the footer reads '14 projects | refreshed 10:58:47 | pending 0' and the top-left reads 'ork ?help') and the logo in the terminal too: a small ASCII or Unicode mark in the TUI header or splash, and a one-line glyph in the ork --version and ork doctor output. A terminal cannot show the SVG, so this slice adds a text version of the chosen mark. The TUI also shows when the daemon's build differs from the TUI's (S46 later note L1: the stale warning is hidden by the alternate screen); the daemon.info call from S46 gives the daemon's build id.

## Why

The version should show where ork runs, which is the terminal. A stale daemon is invisible once the TUI takes the screen.

## Files

- internal/tui (version in the footer or header, title or splash, stale-daemon marker, goldens), internal/cli (version and doctor output), cmd/ork (the build id the TUI is given), internal/daemon/client.go if a typed daemon.info call is needed, tests, docs/dashboard.md.
- The text mark has an ASCII fallback, no colour dependence in monochrome, and fits an 80-column terminal.

## Failing tests

- The TUI shows the ork version (the build id from S46, or the version var) in the footer, and a marker with the daemon's build id when it differs from the TUI's; golden views, colour and monochrome.
- Ask the owner before building: footer or header for the version, splash on start or a permanent header for the mark, and whether the doctor line should carry the mark.
- The TUI title shows the mark in colour and in monochrome; the golden views are updated and reviewed.
- ork --version and ork doctor print the one-line glyph first; --json output is unchanged.
- The mark fits 80 columns and has an ASCII-only fallback used when the terminal is not UTF-8.
